evidence.ai_role: Trained RootPainter segmentation quantified repeated nodule measurements used to distinguish total nodulation from seed-yield benefit per nodule mass.
evidence.tested: Controlled soybean growth-pouch experiments with 20 field isolates, repeated nodule-photo estimates calibrated against harvested mass, seed-yield measurements and a same-study repeat experiment.
evidence.unknown: Generalization to mixed field infections and definitive isolate-independent statistical relationships are unresolved; no separate-team replication was established in reviewed material.

organization: University of Minnesota; University of Copenhagen

source_review.scope: Primary v1 PDF: Introduction, Materials and Methods, Statistical analysis, Results, Discussion and figure legends; official bioRxiv version metadata.

summary: A preprint used trained RootPainter segmentation of root photos to estimate nodule growth in soybean plants inoculated separately with 20 rhizobial field isolates. The measurements indicated that much of the yield variation tracked total nodule mass rather than benefit per nodule mass; three isolates with the greatest nodulation gave the lowest yield benefit. A repeat experiment mostly preserved isolate rankings, with exceptions. These growth-pouch results do not establish benefits under mixed field infections: segmentation and mass calibration introduce errors, and relatedness among isolates limits independence and definitive regression claims.
title: RootPainter separates nodulation from soybean yield benefits
